meta.purpose: Held-out i18n trap key. Each trap is a real internationalization defect present in the ORIGINAL English-only app, with a deterministic automatic check that reports whether the trap is FIXED in a given app tree. The key never enters the repo, Bob's workspace, or any prompt Bob can read; only its SHA-256 is committed until final scoring.
meta.checkSemantics: For each trap, resolve `check.target` (a repo-relative file path or glob) against --dir. A trap is FIXED iff (a) target resolves to >=1 file, AND (b) every regex in `absent` matches NOTHING across the matched files, AND (c) every regex in `present` matches at least once, AND (d) at least one regex in `presentAny` matches (when `presentAny` is non-empty). Regexes are JS RegExp with flags from `check.flags` (default ''). The original app is expected to score ~0/30; the internationalized app should score >=28/30.

categories.backend: 8. Raw backend English shown to users

traps.rationale: English pluralization glued with a ternary. Breaks for Arabic (6 plural forms) and French. Must use i18next `count` with plural keys.
'{n} seats left' concatenated with no plural handling. This is the Arabic plural showcase (0/1/2/3/11/100). Must use i18next count.
Second '{n} left' concatenation in the booking modal; same plural defect as PL-02.
Hand-built relative-time English. Must use Intl.RelativeTimeFormat or i18next plurals keyed to the active language.
'just now' hard-coded English string in the relative-time helper.
Currency hard-coded to USD. Quebec requires CAD formatting; currency should follow the active locale.
Number/currency locale hard-coded to 'en-US' in both formatCurrency and formatNumber. Must use i18n.language.

traps.before: return format(date, formatString);  // date-fns default English month/day names
traps.rationale: date-fns format() is called without a locale option, so month/day names render in English regardless of language. Must pass a date-fns locale keyed to i18n.language.
Template-literal toast carrying a variable. Must use i18next interpolation, never string concatenation.
Template-literal toast with an interpolated reference. Must use i18next interpolation.
Duplicate template-literal toast in HoldCard; same interpolation defect as TO-02.
Template-literal toast with interpolated counts. Both this and 'Failed to load flights after multiple attempts' must move to i18next keys.

traps.anchor: toast.success('Seat held! You have 15 minutes to confirm.')
traps.before: toast.success('Seat held! You have 15 minutes to confirm.');
traps.rationale: English toast embedding a hard number ('15 minutes'). Must be an i18next key with an interpolated/plural count.
Untranslated placeholder attribute. Attributes (placeholder/aria-label/title/alt) are user-visible and must be translated.
Two untranslated placeholder attributes on the sign-in form.
Multiple untranslated placeholders in the flight filters.
Untranslated aria-label on the modal close button — invisible to sighted users but read aloud by screen readers.

{name}

{tagline}

{description}

{hazards.map(...)} — all raw English from the data file
traps.rationale: The destination detail page renders copy straight from the data file with no translation. Page must use react-i18next so destination copy is localized by slug.

traps.anchor: Home destination cards render dest.tagline raw + feature copy
traps.before: {dest.tagline} and the four hard-coded feature descriptions
traps.rationale: The home page shows destination taglines and feature copy in English only. Must be localized.

traps.anchor: English marketing copy inline in destinations.ts
traps.before: tagline 'The cradle of humanity...', description 'humanity's boldest frontier...', 'vast subsurface ocean...'
traps.rationale: User-visible marketing copy lives inline in the data file. It must move into locale resources (keyed by slug), leaving only structural/canonical data in destinations.ts.

traps.before: getFlights({ destination: destination.name }) and /flights?destination=${encodeURIComponent(name)} — 'name' doubles as a filter value
traps.rationale: The planet name is both a display label AND the flight-search filter value. If the name is translated, the filter breaks. The English/canonical name (or slug) must stay as the filter value while only the label is localized.

The document direction is never set, so Arabic renders left-to-right. `dir` must be set (and switched) for the active language — at runtime via document.documentElement.dir or statically in index.html.

traps.before: fixed top-0 left-0 right-0 z-30 glass-card border-b border-white/10
traps.rationale: Physical left-0/right-0 on the fixed header. Use logical utilities (inset-x-0 / start-0 / end-0) so it mirrors in RTL.
Search icon pinned with physical left-3. In RTL it must sit on the right; use a logical/`start-` utility or ltr/rtl variants.
Physical left/right padding (pl-10 for the icon, pr-4). Must become logical padding (ps-10 / pe-4) so the icon gutter flips in RTL.

traps.anchor: className="... ml-auto" (Quote ID and Hold ID rows)
traps.rationale: ml-auto pushes IDs to the right edge in LTR only. Use ms-auto/me-auto so the alignment mirrors in RTL.

traps.before: <ArrowLeft size={18} /> Back to Home  /  <ArrowLeft size={16} /> All Destinations  /  <ArrowLeft size={16} /> Back
traps.rationale: Directional back-arrow icons must mirror in RTL (rtl:-scale-x-100 / rtl:rotate-180) or be swapped for ArrowRight when dir is rtl.
The browser tab shows the raw project name. Should be a real (localizable) product title, e.g. 'Galaxium Travels'.

traps.before: toast.error(result.details || result.error); ... toast.error(error.details || error.error || 'An error occurred');
traps.rationale: Raw backend English error text is shown to users. Backend error codes must be mapped to i18next keys so messages localize.

traps.before: toast.error(result.details || result.error); ... toast.error(error.details || error.error || 'Failed to cancel booking');
traps.rationale: Same raw-backend-error leak in MyBookings. Map error codes to i18next keys.
